response.text:
I can’t give exact month-by-month revenues from the chart without either the image or the underlying data. With only unlabeled gridlines and unlabeled bars, any numbers I give would be guesses — I won’t fabricate exact figures.

What I can do instead (choose one):

1) If you can upload the chart (or paste a screenshot), I will read it and return approximate values with an uncertainty range.  
2) If you can tell me one confirmed reference value (for example: “top gridline = $100k” or “each horizontal gridline = $10k”), I will compute exact month values from the bar heights and tell you how certain those numbers are.  
3) If you need to extract them yourself now, use this quick method to get exact numbers from the image:

- Capture a clear screenshot of the chart (include the full plotting area).  
- Open the screenshot in an image editor that shows pixel coordinates (Paint, Preview, Photoshop, or online image-measure tools).  
- Record the pixel y-coordinate of the top and bottom of the plot area (y_top, y_bottom).  
- Record the pixel y-coordinate of each bar top (y_bar).  
- If you know the numeric range of the y-axis (value_top, value_bottom), compute each bar’s value with:
  value = value_bottom + (value_top - value_bottom) * (y_bottom - y_bar) / (y_bottom - y_top)
- If the y-axis range is unknown but gridlines are evenly spaced, you can (a) count the gridlines N, (b) choose one reasonable assumed unit per gridline, or (c) measure distance between gridlines in pixels and map that to a chosen unit to infer a scale.

Note on uncertainty: results from this method are exact relative to the pixel measurements and the numeric top/bottom values you supply; if you must guess the numeric scale of the axis, the output will be approximate.

Tell me which option you prefer (upload the image, give one known axis value, or I can walk you through the pixel steps), and I’ll proceed.
